#784. Nuno Espírito Santo under threat at West Ham after poor start to the season

Favourites for promotion sit eighth in Championship

Key figures at club losing patience with manager

Nuno Espírito Santo’s future at West Ham is under threat after a disappointing start to the season. West Ham are struggling to live up to their billing as Championship favourites and dropped to eighth after losing 3-1 to West Bromwich Albion on Saturday.

West Ham are intent on an instant return to the Premier League after Nuno failed to save them from relegation last season, but the setback against West Brom put another dent in their promotion push. West Ham occupy the final playoff spot after two consecutive defeats at home and are four points below second placed Swansea City. Nuno is expected to be given time to turn the situation around but key figures have become increasingly impatient. The manager faced unrest from supporters during the West Brom game.

The initial expectation was that Nuno would be fired after taking West Ham down last season. Sources indicated that David Sullivan, the club’s largest shareholder at the time, wanted to part company with the former Nottingham Forest manager. Daniel Kretinsky, the Czech billionaire, was in Nuno’s corner and is understood to have argued for continuity.

Sullivan then resigned as a joint-chair and director of West Ham to fight what he described as “false allegations” concerning his personal conduct. Kretinsky became West Ham’s biggest shareholder in September, buying a stake of 46%. The agreement saw Sullivan, who is not on the board, increase his stake from 38% to 40%.

Any decision on Nuno’s future will be a collective board decision. Karim Virani, the interim CEO, and Nils Koppen, the director of recruitment, will have their say. West Ham, who visit Cardiff City on Wednesday, are unhappy after a run of two wins in six games and Nuno is likely to face difficult questions if he cannot inspire an improvement before this month’s international break.

West Ham turned to Nuno after firing Graham Potter in September 2025. The 52-year-old’s tactics and signings did not convince last season and the problems have continued since relegation. West Ham sold Crysencio Summerville and Mateus Fernandes after going down but they held on to Jarrod Bowen and Tomas Soucek. They broke the EFL transfer record when they signed Arne Engels from Celtic for £22m.

The feeling within West Ham is that they have the best squad in the Championship and should be playing better. But Nuno has struggled to settle on his best 11 and various problems have emerged. West Ham have kept three clean sheets in 13 games. They have started games slowly, conceding the first goal on six occasions.

Their strikers – Joel Piroe, Pablo Felipe and Taty Castellanos – all joined under Nuno and have five league goals between them this season. Bowen is the top scorer with seven but West Ham lack a clear playing identity and have not found the right balance in midfield. The squad contains two holding midfielders but Soungoutou Magassa and Edson Alvarez are both out of favour.

West Ham still hope that Nuno can lead a push up the table. There have been some positive signs, including 6-0 wins over Wrexham and Lincoln City, although the latter were reduced to nine men in the first half. West Ham’s best performance of the season was their gritty 1-0 win away to Swansea, suggesting they are better when there is less pressure on them to dominate games.

#783. Martha Stewart “Distressed” Over Homeless Halloween Costume Backlash

After Martha Stewart sparked backlash with a since-deleted post featuring her dressed as a homeless person for Halloween, she said she was trying to bring awareness to the “serious subject.”

After the lifestyle guru sparked backlash by posting a photo of herself dressed as a homeless person for Halloween, she expressed her remorse over the controversy and detailed what she had intended with the since-deleted post.

“I’ve spent decades teaching others how to celebrate Halloween—sharing fun, festive recipes, providing unique craft ideas and giving tips on entertaining and hosting” Stewart said in a statement to People on Nov. 1, “to make the most of one of my favorite holidays of the year.”

As such, she explained, “I am distressed that my Halloween costume yesterday, which was intended to bring more awareness to the very serious subject of homelessness, has offended people, which was never my intention.”

In the photo—posted around social media before Stewart deleted—the Martha Stewart Show alum wore torn jean and a plaid button-up under a torn button-up. She completed the look with a beanie, dirt on her face, and a sign on a clipboard reading, “I AM HUNGRY HELP ME!!” (The caption of the post encouraged followers to shop from her QVC candle line.)

The 85-year-old went on to highlight the ways in which homelessness has been a cause close to her heart.

“Homelessness continues to remain one of America’s greatest challenges and ongoing crises,” she continued, “something that I care deeply about and I have spent a significant amount of time and effort supporting charities that combat this ongoing social epidemic.”

And despite the misstep now, she emphasized, “I am committed to continuing to make a difference.”

E! News has reached out to Stewart for comment but has not heard back.

With decades in the public eye, Stewart is no stranger to occasionally stepping in it, though from her experience it’s best to keep one’s head held high. After all, as she admitted in 2013, "I've never hit a bottom, just bumps in the road."

This latest bump in the road behind her soon enough, read on for a look back at some of her most jaw-dropping confessions…

Martha Stewart—then still Martha Kostyra—lost her virginity when she was 19, to her future husband Andrew Stewart, a student at Yale Law School.

“He was very aggressive,” the lifestyle mogul said in the 2024 Netflix documentary Martha, “and I liked it.”

Martha Stewart Kissed Another Man—on Her Honeymoon

It wasn’t a harbinger of good things to come, but Martha maintained that kissing another man while she and Andrew were honeymooning in Europe after their 1961 nuptials wasn’t that big a deal.

“It was neither naughty nor unfaithful,” she said in Martha of smooching the stranger at a cathedral on Easter eve in Florence, Italy. “It was just emotional, of the moment. That’s how I looked at it. And it was exciting. I wish we could all experience such an evening.”

Martha Stewart Cheated on Husband Andrew Stewart

Martha admitted in the documentary to a “very brief affair” with “a very attractive Irish man” during her time working as a stockbroker in the late 1960s.

“I would have never broken up a marriage for it,” she said. “It was nothing. It was like the kiss in the cathedral.”

She insinuated that Andrew was repeatedly unfaithful, despite her ex-husband maintaining he didn’t cheat until she confessed her infidelity.

“I didn’t go run off with people. He was running off with people,” she said. “I always said I was a swan and like all swans, they are monogamous.”

Being a Mom Wasn’t a Natural Fit for Martha Stewart

Martha had to work at honing her maternal instincts when her daughter Alexis Stewart was born in 1965.

“Back then, everybody was having babies so young,” she reflected in Martha. “That was sort of the style and the habit. I thought it was a natural thing, and it turns out it’s not at all nature to be a mother.”

While she and Alexis remain close, Martha told People in 2020, “I tried to involve her in everything, but the minute she could leave home and go to boarding school, she did. Our relationship has always been a difficult mother-daughter relationship. Difficult, but she would do anything for me, and I would do anything for her."

Martha infamously served five months at FPC Alderson after being convicted in 2004 of conspiracy, obstruction and lying to federal investigators in connection with an insider trading case.

At one point she was punished for touching a female guard’s “big silver key chain” after complimenting how nice the guard looked, as she shared in Martha, having momentarily forgotten the prison rules.

She ended up “dragged into solitary for ‘touching an officer,’” Martha said. “No food or water for a day. This was ‘Camp Cupcake,’ remember?”

Martha Stewart’s Thoughts on Hosting a Talk Show

Upon her release in March 2005, as Martha put it in the doc, she “had to climb out of a f--king hole”—and daytime TV seemed like a step in that direction.

But while she’s been the face of countless endeavors over the years, onscreen and off, hosting Martha for seven seasons, she said, “was more like prison than being at Alderson.”

Martha said on a February 2024 episode of her eponymous podcast that she never had a facelift, but her dermatologist Dr. Daniel Belkin did inject Botox in her neck and along her jawline and put filler in her cheeks and jawline.

Belkin noted that they had also done ultrasound-based skin tightening, and she recalled having a Fraxel laser treatment on her body.

"My décolletage and across my chest looks so good now," Martha told the doctor. "That is a combination of your work and Pilates." She further chalked up her radiant visage to clean eating—her daily green juice ingredients come straight from her garden, naturally—and staying active.

Martha Stewart Enjoys Snoop Dogg’s Contact High

While she didn’t partake herself, Martha felt “fabulous” when her friend and frequent cohost Snoop Dogg smoked weed around her, she shared when he was a guest on the 2022 premiere of her podcast.

“It makes me feel really good," she confessed. "It does not disturb my concentration. In fact, I think it makes it even better and it doesn't make me tired or any of the things people say marijuana does to you. It's fantastic, I think it's great."

The Alcohol Martha Stewart Hadn’t Tasted Since College

Martha loves a craft cocktail, but there’s one spirit that has haunted her since she was a student at Barnard.

“I got so drunk on gin in college,” she told Snoop in 2024 at Food Network's New York City Wine & Food Festival, “that I have not ever had gin since.”

"But," she told her friend, who inevitably entered the alcohol market with the drink he's been linked to for 30 years, "I can’t wait to taste your Gin & Juice!”

Incidentally, though Martha is practically synonymous with white wine, she is not a day drinker.

“I never drink it before dinner, ever," she told The Cut in 2017. "I couldn't function for a second if I had to drink it at lunchtime or something like that."

Why Martha Stewart Doesn’t Wear Underwear

Martha skips wearing underwear in lieu of having her swimsuit on at all times—just in case she feels like taking a dip.

"Bathing suits are my underwear," the 2023 Sports Illustrated Swimsuit Issue cover girl told Page Six in 2024. "I don't wear any of that structured stuff. No tight lace. I don't wear those. I only wear Eres bathing suits under my clothes."

Martha Stewart’s One-Night Stand Confession

On Watch What Happens Live! in 2013, the answer was “yes” when Andy Cohen asked if Martha ever had a one-night stand. She had also sexted, FYI, and her answer to whether she’d ever had a threesome was a smirking “maybe.”

#781. From VHS dreams to San Siro glory: Amorim’s Milan surge puts rivals on notice | Nicky Bandini

Inspired by the legendary Milan sides of his youth, the manager gave his side a lift with a tactical victory over Inter

Ruben Amorim had waited a lifetime for his first Milan derby. As a kid growing up in Lisbon, he supported two football teams. There was the local one, Benfica, whose games he attended so early in life that his father has recalled changing nappies in the stands of the old Estádio da Luz. And the other one that captivated him from overseas.

“I remember watching tapes of that Milan team with [Paolo] Maldini, [Franco] Baresi, [Ruud] Gullit, [Frank] Rijkaard, [Dejan] Savicevic,” Amorim told Portuguese newspaper Expresso back in 2017. “My childhood dreams were to play for Benfica and Milan. I’ve fulfilled one. Now I suppose I’ll have to become a coach for the other!”

It took him another nine years to achieve that ambition. The Milan side he inherited this June did not look like the continental conquerors he used to admire on VHS. This version had just missed out on the Champions League for a second season running. Its hoped-for star of this decade, Rafael Leão, was ready to move on amid laments of unfulfilled potential.

Still, from day one, Amorim has given off the air of a cat who got the cream. It was tempting to infer some relief at moving on from an unhappy chapter at Manchester United. Certainly it can’t have hurt that Milan’s owners backed their new manager to a tune of more than €160m on transfer fees in the summer window.

But there was something in there too, of a person fulfilling a promise they made to their younger self. “Everybody knows Milan is one of my clubs since I was a boy,” said Amorim. “In my time as a young boy, Milan was the strongest team in Italy. And calcio was the best league in the world.”

Serie A lost that title some time ago. No Italian team has won the Champions League since 2010, and no player representing one has been awarded the Ballon d’Or since 2007. The Premier League long ago surpassed all rival competitions for TV revenues and spending power. Only a handful of super clubs elsewhere have kept up.

And yet, Serie A is having some kind of moment. Its reputation as the home of dour catenaccio is as outdated as Amorim’s old VCR, but things have spun especially far in the opposite direction this season, with an average of 3.18 goals per game. Italy’s top division has become home to some of the giddiest attacking football on the continent. Through almost 10 completed rounds there have been two 0-0 draws.

Bologna 2-1 Monza, Udinese 2-5 Roma, Milan 3-1 Inter, Como 1-0 Venezia, Frosinone 2-0 Torino, Lazio 2-1 Cagliari, Lecce 1-2 Genoa, Juventus 2-0 Napoli

Monday: Sassuolo v Fiorentina (5.30pm GMT), Atalanta v Parma (7.45pm GMT)

Amorim’s Milan have played their part. On Wednesday night they suffered their first league defeat, a barmy 4-2 loss at home to Bologna in which they fell behind early, came back to lead before half-time then collapsed after the interval. Their manager cited exhaustion. An ominous thought, leading into Saturday’s derby. Inter had dropped just two points all season. Even their one draw felt more like a win, coming from two goals down to get a result away to Roma. Reigning champions, who reinforced the deepest squad in Serie A with the English trio of Curtis Jones, John Stones and Djed Spence in the summer, the Nerazzurri have been strong favourites to retain their title.

But after waiting a lifetime for a part in this fixture, Amorim was never going to arrive unprepared. If anything, the loss to Bologna might have been influenced by his keeping one eye on the derby. Luka Modric and Christian Pulisic were both left out of the starting XI in midweek, coming on only as second-half substitutes. Both lined up at kick-off against Inter. So did several other starters who had been deemed unfit even for a place on the bench against Bologna – Mario Gila, Adrien Rabiot and Diego Moreira. Amorim sprung a surprise on top of that by naming the 20-year-old Sankhoun Diawara, whose only previous Milan start had been at centre-back, as his left wing-back in a 3-4-2-1.

The manager has shown more tactical flexibility at Milan than he did in Manchester, alternating his back three with a four. In the biggest game of his Milan tenure to date, however, Amorim returned to what he knows best. And Cristian Chivu copied him.

Inter’s manager was grappling with an availability crisis up front. Lautaro Martínez has been out for weeks with a hamstring strain, while Francesco Pio Esposito and Ange-Yoan Bonny were unfit to start due to a virus. Chivu adapted by pushing Andy Diouf, a former midfielder who has been thriving at wing-back, forward to play on the right shoulder of Marcus Thuram, with Petar Sucic on the left.

But where the Nerazzurri looked unsure of themselves in a new system, Milan were straight into their stride. Pulisic put them in front in the fourth minute, his thumping header from Moreira’s cross the culmination of 80 seconds of unbroken possession. Rabiot then made it 2-0 in the 10th minute with a magnificent first-time flick across his body at a corner.

Inter’s defending, on both occasions, was horrendous, but that can be acknowledged without diminishing Milan’s design. The Rabiot goal was a rehearsed training ground routine, Diawara crossing paths with the Frenchman and blocking Hakan Calhanoglu’s attempts to track. Moreira was also flawless in his deliveries. The derby became his breakout moment, showing why Milan spent more than €50m to sign him from Strasbourg this summer.

Inter have recovered from losing positions five times already in this Serie A season, and three times from 2-0 down. They were threatening to repeat the trick after Alessandro Bastoni pulled a goal back from a corner. Spence forced a sensational save from Mike Maignan. But Milan won a free-kick, 20 yards out on the right. Moreira asked Modric to let him take it, then whipped a left-footed shot over the wall into the near side of the net.

The game finished 3-1 to Milan, Inter’s first league defeat and a huge lift for Amorim. Despite being unbeaten themselves before the midweek loss to Bologna, the Rossoneri have not always convinced. Even when controlling the tempo of games, they seem to lack clarity in the final third. Gonçalo Ramos, the club’s record signing, has not looked a natural fit as a lone striker, dropping deep too often when his team needs a presence inside the box. He has scored just twice in 10 starts since his €73m from Paris Saint-Germain.

Even this win raised questions. Can it really be the long-term vision for Moreira, the right wing-back, to frequently hold a position on the pitch higher than the centre-forward?

Amorim was quick to insist that nobody should get carried away on Saturday. He expressed delight for supporters and described the experience of his first Milan derby as unlike any other game he had ever been a part of. But he also said Milan had only been good, not great, and noted that the three points here were only the same number they would have got by beating Bologna.

A sensible line to take. Milan have dominated this fixture lately – winning the last four derbies across all competitions and staying unbeaten in the last eight. Yet they have not finished above their neighbours since 2021-22, their last Scudetto-winning campaign.

Still, beating your greatest rival is always better than the alternative. The club’s owner, Gerry Cardinale, has been vocal in backing the new manager, telling La Gazzetta dello Sport last week that he was all in on “Amorim ball”. But in the week that Milan and Inter jointly presented plans for the new stadium that will replace San Siro in 2031, this result added weight to his assertion that the Rossoneri can contend for a Scudetto too.

#778. From rotten food to political opponents: Researchers explore how disgust relates to our beliefs, and why the connection is complicated

Some studies have linked disgust sensitivity to socially conservative attitudes. But ahead of the US midterm elections, does disgust shape our politics, or do our beliefs shape what we find disgusting?

Some studies have linked disgust sensitivity to socially conservative attitudes. But ahead of the US midterm elections, does disgust shape our politics, or do our beliefs shape what we find disgusting?

The smell of rotten food can make us recoil. Certain sexual practices can provoke a similar reaction. And in today's polarized political climate, even political opponents can become objects of disgust.

Psychologists have long investigated whether sensitivity to disgust helps explain political beliefs. A review of 24 studies found that people who reported being more easily disgusted tended to hold more socially conservative views.

"We think that it evolved in part to reduce exposure to things that could make you sick," psychologist Yoel Inbar, of the University of British Columbia in Canada, told DW.

But disgust is not a single emotion. The Three-Domain Disgust Scale, developed in 2009, distinguishes three types:

One theory is that people who are especially wary of germs and disease may also prefer traditional social rules.

Inbar explains that avoiding potential sources of infection can also mean missing out on new experiences.

"Some people are more on the cautious conservative side, and some people are more on the exploring risk-taking side when it comes to pathogen exposure," he said.

Indeed, the language of contamination also appears in political rhetoric. During his 2024 presidential campaign, Donald Trump repeatedly described immigrants as "poisoning the blood of our country." Trump has also described himself as a "germaphobe."

Inbar acknowledges that the evidence linking sensitivity to disgust with conservative political beliefs remains uncertain.

"We have hypotheses. I don't know that we have as strong of evidence as I would like," Inbar said.

Disgust is not exclusively conservative. And what people find revolting can depend on their values.

A 2020 study titled "Is Disgust a "Conservative" Emotion?" found that liberals and conservatives were disgusted by different things.

Conservatives, generally aligned with the Republicans in US politics, reported greater disgust at examples involving sexual behaviors and drug use, while liberals, generally aligned with the Democrats, reported greater disgust at animal abuse and environmental pollution.

However, when asked how easily disgusted they were in general, there was no clear difference across the political spectrum.

Some early studies suggested conservatives showed stronger physical reactions to frightening or disgusting images, measured partly through changes in sweating.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

But subsequent research, including a 2020 study by political psychologist Bert Bakker at the University of Amsterdam, struggled to reproduce those findings.

Studies based on questionnaires, however, have generally found that people with more conservative attitudes report being more easily disgusted.

"If bodily reactions don't differ across political groups, why do feelings?" Manos Tsakiris, of Royal Holloway and the Centre for the Politics of Feelings at the University of London, told DW.

Tsakiris and colleague Mariana von Mohr wondered whether the answer might lie in how people perceive and interpret signals from their bodies.

Scientists call the perception of internal sensations, such as hunger, breathing or a racing heart, "interoception." It's sometimes called our eighth sense, alongside the familiar five, plus our senses of balance and body position.

"A bodily signal doesn't arrive with a label attached," Tsakiris told DW. "We have to notice it and make sense of it."

The researchers surveyed 632 US adults, asking how much they noticed and trusted signals from their bodies — a measure known as "interoceptive sensibility."

They found that people who were more easily disgusted by sexual behavior tended to be more conservative, regardless of how aware they felt of their bodies.

But for moral disgust, the link to conservatism was found only among people who reported lower bodily awareness.

What particularly surprised Tsakiris was that perceived bodily awareness alone had no link to political views.

"People who are highly attuned to their bodies were neither more liberal nor more conservative," he said.

Inbar questions whether all forms of disgust are equally useful for studying political attitudes.

He and Joshua Tybur, one of the creators of the Three-Domain Disgust Scale, generally prefer measuring pathogen disgust — reactions to potential sources of disease — rather than sexual disgust.

Questions about sexual disgust may already reflect conservative beliefs about sex.

"It's almost asking people the same thing twice," Inbar said.

The new study found no significant link between pathogen disgust and conservative views.

Inbar wants the findings on bodily awareness and disgust tested again, with predictions set out in advance. For now, he considers them "suggestive at best."

Tsakiris suggests that people who struggle to understand their bodily feelings may be more vulnerable to political messages telling them what those feelings mean.

"I know what you're feeling. You're feeling angry or you're feeling disgusted about this thing," he said, illustrating how someone might put an emotional label on another person's unease.

Such labels could influence political behavior, he argues, although the study did not directly test this.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

"This is how disgust can do political work: it can turn moral judgments about individuals into judgments about whole groups," he said.

The research cannot establish whether disgust shapes political beliefs or existing beliefs shape what people find disgusting. Bakker notes that political beliefs can influence how people describe their own personalities, suggesting the relationship could work both ways.

"Voting behavior is very complex and citizens make up their mind about politics in a complex way," he told DW.

Inbar also cautions against exaggerating disgust's importance. "The thing to emphasize in your story is that the relationship, while it's consistent, is quite small," he said.

"It's one of the many influences on people's politics."

Tsakiris advocates what he calls "critical feeling": questioning our emotional responses to provocative material, including social media posts, just as we question the information itself.

He also emphasizes discussing our feelings with others and listening to different perspectives, even when we disagree.

"Life and politics and democracy is a contact sport," he said. Edited by: Rosalie Delaney

#777. ‘We had to dig in’: Arsenal’s Anfield win was performance of champions, says Rice

Midfielder praises his side’s grit and determination

Szoboszlai says there are fine margins between sides

Declan Rice says Arsenal are ready for more grinding wins as he hailed the 1-0 success at Liverpool on Sunday as the performance of champions. The midfielder set up Kai Havertz for the only goal on 16 minutes but his defensive work was arguably more impressive; his physicality and reading of the game.

Liverpool were unhappy at the non-award of a penalty for a Jürrien Timber shirt-pull on Alexander Isak in the 21st minute and it was a day when the Kop fumed about Arsenal’s streetwise tactics, especially how they won free-kicks – albeit their own players were also guilty of going down too easily at times. The Arsenal goalkeeper, David Raya, was booked for time-wasting in the 92nd minute as his team closed out the victory.

Arsenal won 1-0 at Nottingham Forest in their previous Premier League away match – after which they were criticised for their lack of creativity. This time, the barbs centred on their gamesmanship because they were a threat on the counterattack. They are not about to trouble anybody connected to the club.

“No game is plain sailing; it is always going to be tough,” Rice said. “Looking back at that Forest game, it wasn’t the best performance but we ground it out, we won and there’s going to be more of that this season. But results like this one [at Liverpool] just make it that extra bit special so we are delighted.”

It was Arsenal’s first league victory at Anfield since 2012 and they have won at four grounds where they did not win when securing the title last season, the others being Villa Park, the Stadium of Light and the City Ground. “Any team who has won at Anfield in the past has never had it easy,” Rice said. “We had to dig in and give it everything because they throw so many attacks at you. We had to be resilient and strong. It was a great win.”

Rice was asked whether it was a match in which Arsenal had played like champions. “For sure,” he replied. “It’s just drilled into us. What the manager [Mikel Arteta] has built at this club and the togetherness of the lads – you don’t get that performance without the lads being all together.

“The way the manager has everything under control, the way everyone works towards everything he wants is not like anything I’ve ever seen before. So credit to us for what we have been doing for the last few years. Now it’s a massive thing to deliver again this year.”

Dominik Szoboszlai said Liverpool’s defeat demonstrated there were only fine margins between Andoni Iraola’s side and the Premier League champions.

Liverpool failed to register a shot on target in a Premier League home game for the first time since records began in 2003-04, according to Opta, as Arsenal moved three points clear at the summit. Szoboszlai believes the contest turned on the Isak shirt-pull incident and that there was little between the teams.

Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football

“We are just one penalty less and that’s a big difference,” said the midfielder. “You know Anfield, you know our quality. I know they are a great team but it wouldn’t be easy for them [to have come back from a successful penalty].”

Iraola claimed he would tell Liverpool players to go down in the box but Szoboszlai said that was not their style.

“I don’t think in this moment you can think: ‘Oh, let me wait for someone touching me and I’ll fall down,’” he said. “No, Alex is focusing on the ball and he wants to head the ball in the net … It’s a penalty. I don’t know what they expect from us, to dive or something? I don’t think we are the type of team or players to do that but from now on we might need to do it. If Alex falls down it’s a clear penalty. Timber doesn’t really care about the ball and maybe if he doesn’t pull Alex’s shirt Alex can head it in the goal.”

#776. Influencer Liam Fitzgerald Dead at 29 After Motorcycle Crash

Fitness and lifestyle influencer Liam Fitzgerald died on early Oct. 30 after a motorcycle accident, his girlfriend Jamie Lyn Rinaldi shared, noting that he had “suffered severe injuries.” He was 29.

Liam Fitzgerald’s loved ones are expressing their grief.

The lifestyle influencer died in the early morning of Oct. 30 from injuries sustained during a motorcycle accident, his girlfriend Jamie Lyn Rinaldi confirmed. He was 29.

“He suffered severe injuries, and despite the efforts of those who tried desperately to save him, they were unable to bring him back,” Rinaldi wrote on Instagram on Oct. 31 alongside a photo of Fitzgerald. “There are no words to describe the heartbreak of this loss. This is an incredibly difficult and heartbreaking time of everyone who knew and loved him.”

Fitzgerald, who boasted a million followers on Instagram and over 350 thousand on TikTok, was best known for his workout and wellness content, often also sharing motivational videos. In their own statement, posted to his Instagram on Nov. 1, his family honored the “shining light.”

“He had a way of lighting up every room he walked into, a personality impossible to forget, and a heart that loved deeply,” they wrote. “From family and friends to teammates, strangers, and people around the world, he inspired so many. He loved his people fiercely and would protect them with everything he had.”

Highlighting how important his work was to him, his loved ones detailed his passion for his content creation work, and what he hoped to achieve with it. They also didn’t shy away from the more difficult moments in his life.

“Liam had his own struggles, too,” the statement, signed Penny, Natalie, Dermot and Bethany as well as Rinaldi, continued. “He battled with alcohol on and off and knew it was hurting him. This is shared in the hope that his story reaches someone who needs it. If you're fighting that battle, please stay strong, reach out to your loved ones, and ask for help. You don't have to fight alone. Keep going.”

Emphasizing that he “never pretended to be” perfect, they noted how “Fitzgerald “always strived to grow and do better. He had dreams, ambitions, and so much more life to live.”

And now, they are left grieving what his next chapter could have been. “He had just turned 29. So many places to see, memories to make, and people to love,” the Fitzgeralds noted. “His life was tragically cut short in a motorcycle accident, leaving behind a heartbreak that words will never be able to describe.”

“His laughter, energy, accomplishments, and the memories he created will live on through everyone he touched,” the added before ending with a heartbreaking reminder. “Hug your people tighter, tell them you love them, forgive when you can, and never assume you have more time.”

As Rinaldi grieves, she was also candid about where she and Fitzgerald stood after facing some recent ups and downs, with her sharing a lengthy statement hoping to “clarify a few things so everyone understands.”

“Ever since I got to Florida, Liam and I reconnected,” the 30-year-old told followers in her Nov. 1 Instagram Story, alongside a photo of her and Fitzgerald. “He apologized, wanted to make things right, and showed me every single day that he was willing to put in the effort to change. I love this man, and I chose to give him another chance. I forgave him, and we were working on building something beautiful together again.”

And they purposefully kept a lot of this out of the public eye.

“We spent so much time together and chose to keep our relationship private because social media can be overwhelming, and we wanted to focus on us without outside opinions,” she explained. So, after privately working on their relationship, “Just a few days ago, we officially decided to be boyfriend and girlfriend again. We were happy, making progress and excited about the future we were building together.”

So, she’s still trying to make sense of this tragedy.

“Please understand that this is the hardest thing I have ever had to face. Losing someone you love so deeply and so suddenly is unimaginable,” Rinaldi shared. “My heart is completely broken, and the last thing needed right now is judgement, assumptions, or speculation about our relationship.”

She added, “I loved Liam with all my heart. What we shared was real, it was special and from day one, he had a place in my heart that nobody else could ever fill.”

#774. Dazn secures exclusive deal on global streaming rights for 2029 Club World Cup

Deal deepens company’s relationship with Fifa

Dazn paid $1bn for global rights for the 2025 tournament

Dazn has secured an exclusive option for global streaming rights for the next men’s Club World Cup in 2029 in a development that deepens its partnership with Fifa.

The Saudi Arabia-backed streaming company came to Fifa’s aid before the inaugural 32-team Club World Cup in the United States last year by agreeing to pay $1bn for global rights for the tournament after many linear broadcasters and other streamers had declined to bid.

Apple TV had held talks with Fifa over a global streaming deal for 2025, but withdrew owing to a disagreement over valuation, and Fifa’s subsequent attempt to sell the rights on a regional basis foundered.

Dazn’s surprise late bid, facilitated by the purchase of a 10% stake in the company by Saudi’s Surj Sports Investment group, in effect bankrolled Fifa’s $1bn (£745m) prize fund, with the winners, Chelsea, taking home about $114m (£85m).

In the Guardian app, tap the Profile settings button at the top right, then select Notifications. Turn on sport notifications.

If you already have the Guardian app, make sure you’re on the most recent version.

If you don't have the Guardian app, download it from the iOS App Store on iPhone or the Google Play store on Android by searching for 'The Guardian'.

The value of its Club World Cup rights deal, or the point at which the option must be triggered, is not known but will give Fifa breathing space before the second edition of its expanded competition that has been designed as a major money spinner but remains fraught with political problems.

Planning for the 2029 tournament has proved difficult, with no decisions made on venues, format or size despite longstanding discussions between Fifa and the clubs about expanding to 48 teams, first reported by the Guardian two years ago.

Club World Cup progress has been a casualty of the fallout from Gianni Infantino’s aborted World Cup sell-off proposal, which led the lobby group European Football Clubs (EFC) to threaten to withdraw its support.

In a letter to Fifa obtained by the Guardian EFC also expressed “serious disappointment” at the delays in paying $250m in solidarity money owed to clubs from 2025 more than a year after the first competition had concluded.

Relations between EFC and Fifa are understood to have improved since the withdrawal of Infantino’s Fifa Forward Enterprise plan, but they have yet to agree the finer details of a proposed joint venture to manage the Club World Cup’s commercial operations, which may be put on hold until after the Fifa presidential election in March.

Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football

The 2030 World Cup co-hosts Morocco will be the favourites to host in 2029 if Infantino is re-elected given his close relationship with King Mohammed VI.

Fifa’s decision to award hosting rights to the first women’s Club World Cup to the United States, revealed by the Guardian last month, has strengthened Morocco’s case because the US was in the running for 2029.

A jointly hosted tournament staged by Morocco and Spain is another possibility. Portugal, the third major 2030 co-hosts, are understood to have reservations about hosting.

#773. Pete Davidson, Ex Elsie Hewitt Reunite For Daughter's First Halloween

Pete Davidson and his ex Elsie Hewitt came together to celebrate their daughter Scottie’s first Halloween, with the family dressing up as Sopranos characters for the occasion.

Pete Davidson and Elsie Hewitt are bringing out the gabagools, not goblins for their daughter’s first Halloween.

More than five months after the former couple broke up, they reunited to celebrate the holiday with their baby girl Scottie, 10 months, stepping out in an epic Sopranos-themed family costume.

Alongside her Nov. 1 Instagram carousel of photos, Hewitt shared a punny reference to the HBO drama, captioning her post, “smells like halloween.”

And for her little one’s first Halloween, Scottie was dressed as Tony Soprano himself. But she didn’t just wear any simple costume.

After all, the tiny tot—who was born in December 2025—adorably donned a robe as she rode in a wagon with a blue blanket on her lap, while surrounded by a yellow rubber ducky and stuffed animal ducks, with her costume appearing to be a nod to Tony (the late James Gandolfini) relaxing in a jacuzzi.

And Scottie’s parents proved they paid extra attention to detail as she also had a fake stuffed cigar in tow, an essential for any mini mobster, along with a light-up LED sign that read “Bada Bing!”—a nod to the fictional strip club in The Sopranos—attached to her ride.

As she cannoli-ed the competition with her costume, Hewitt, 30, and Davidson, 32, also joined in on the fun, with the former pair—who split in May after a little over a year of dating—dressing as other Sopranos characters.

Hewitt sported a dark red track suit, neck brace and dark sunglasses for her costume as Christopher Moltisanti (Michael Imperioli). As for Davidson, meanwhile, he dressed as Paulie Walnuts (Tony Sirico), donning track pants and a leather jacket, adding silver-white wings to his dark hair for a finishing touch.

And while the model and Saturday Night Live alum are no longer together, they’ve shed light on the importance of having a healthy co-parenting relationship.

“We are cooperatively co-parenting our daughter whose well-being remains our top priority,” Davidson and Hewitt shared in a joint statement through their reps to Page Six in July, “and we are fully committed to working together to give her love from both of us.”

And since kicking off their parenthood journey last year, the pair have continued to open up about the special experience.

“Scottie is my whole life,” Davidson told Variety in September. “I was living or dying on this business and what I thought people thought of me. It was all validation and ‘If I do this, then I’ll do that.’ But as soon as I saw her for the first time, I was like, ‘Oh my God, none of this f--kin’ matters at all. It’s a job. If I get to do cool stuff, great; if not, cool, I get to be home more with my kid.’”

#772. Falkirk brick wall Bain boosts Scotland chances

Falkirk goalkeeper Scott Bain produced an outstanding performance in the 2-0 win over Celtic

Scott Bain must be praying that Scotland head coach Sebastien Pocognoli was watching on as Falkirk ended a 19-year wait to beat Celtic.

The former Celtic goalkeeper was imperious, unbeatable, as Falkirk ran out 2-0 winners to earn a fourth win on the bounce and reach fourth place in the Scottish Premiership.

An absolute brick wall as he earned a third clean sheet in a row.

Not that all the praise should go his way. Everyone in Bairns blue delivered, but Bain was inspired, making save after save to deny Celtic on a day that will go down in Falkirk folklore. One that intensified the pressure on Martin O'Neill's side.

With the Scotland squad for the upcoming Nations League fixtures announced this week, surely Bain has enhanced his chances of pushing for not just a place in the squad but potentially the chance to stake a claim for a starting role.

Listen: Derby delight for Hibs, fresh questions for Celtic

Are Celtic club in regression amid run of six defeats in 10?

Impressive Falkirk earn first win over hapless Celtic in 19 years

Bain made nine saves against Celtic, with a number of them outstanding, as his side kept a clean sheet for the third game in a row.

That's now a run of 342 minutes without conceding a goal for the Bairns.

"Scott Bain was unbelievable," former Celtic goalkeeper Pat Bonner enthused. "Absolutely unbelievable.

"It was a terrific display from Falkirk defensively. Falkirk deserve it. They've got a terrific young team."

Bain himself explained how he felt as he zoned in on repelling Celtic no matter what they threw at him.

"I felt really confident in the game," he said. "I felt confident in the players and the game plan and I knew that I would be called upon, but it just felt like one of those days where they weren't going to score.

"You can't really get a better day as a goalkeeper than thinking that you're not going to be beaten. So, really, really pleased for my own performance, but more so pleased for the team. It's a fantastic step in the right direction."

The Scotland international extended his Falkirk contract in January and is tied to the club until the summer of 2028, with the option of a further year.

At the time, manager John McGlynn stated that "he's been outstanding from the moment he walked into the club".

After this fabulous display, he lavished even more praise on his number one, who turns 35 this month.

"Scott Bain had two really outstanding saves [in the first half] and there might have been another very good save, but there weren't as many as there were in the second half where he had to continuously produce," he said.

"So a huge thank you to Scott for the actual game he's had today."

No talk of that just being his job but genuine thanks for a memorable afternoon that went a long way to delivering a memorable win.

Bain took a step out of his comfort zone as back-up at Celtic. A sizeable drop in salary to pursue his ambition of regular game time. Days like this surely make that decision justified.

With Scotland lacking the sort of goalkeeping depth they enjoyed for so many years, displays like this can certainly do no harm.

There's an argument that Bain, outside of his shot-stopping ability that was on full display against Celtic, has the type of composure with his feet that may suit Pocognoli's approach.

"I think I've performed well since the last camp and I think I've been performing well throughout the season," Bain added.

"So I would hope to be in it [Scotland squad]. I really enjoyed the last camp. I really enjoyed the way the manager worked and seeing what he wants from his team.

"I'd be delighted if I can get back in and experience more time with him."

This time, the four-time capped goalkeeper may have enhanced his chances of adding to that tally.

#771. Hibs toast win over Hearts - but will they kick on before cup final?

Hibs players joined their fans in a stirring rendition of Sunshine On Leith

Such were Marink Reedijk's wishes, shared in an official Hibernian video, external from the dressing room following their historic Hampden beating of Heart of Midlothian in the Scottish League Cup semi-final.

If the Hibs head coach ventured into Leith on Sunday night he would not have been short of offers for both, as he has instantly scribbled his name into the history books.

His wait for a first win in charge ended at game five. As player of the match Joe Newell said afterwards: "I would have taken four losses if this was the way it clicked."

There was a wee wait for Reedjik to break his Hibs duck, but that is nothing compared to the agony Hibs supporters had endured since 2006 when travelling across the M8 to face their city rivals at the national stadium.

Four visits, four endings with jubilant Jambos. Until now.

The sights and sounds of Sunshine on Leith being belted from the east end of the national stadium will take some time to shift, for this is a win Hibs must savour.

Self-professed "ice king" Reedijk revelled in the iconic anthem but admitted it is his responsibility to make "rational decisions" and so remove himself from the "lovely atmosphere".

He will know he and his players must make this moment the launchpad as they attempt to lift off the bottom of the Scottish Premiership.

After he has enjoyed the tunes and pints, of course.

Hibs edge Hearts in thrilling derby to reach League Cup final

Giant curiosity Hibs finally liberated from the sucker punch

McInnes demands more after delivering Rangers' trophy chance

Who could have thought it would have played out this way?

On the eve of their big trip west, Hibs had slipped - again - to the foot of the league table after Kilmarnock picked up a point at home to the 10 men of St Johnstone.

A shocking place for this squad to be, but it was - temporarily - rendered meaningless 24 hours later.

Given their turbulent start to the season - missing out on Europe, failing to win at home and changing managers - being backed by 19,000 supporters was something in itself.

Finally, they were rewarded. Those who travelled to Warsaw last year to lose out on goal difference to Legia and returned from Gent in August with an abundance of hope only to have it dashed at Easter Road, had their moment of joy. And they rightly milked it.

When Jordi Altena's deep free-kick in the 93rd minute ended in goalkeeper Raphael Sallinger's hands, the roar from the other end of Hampden shook the steps on which Hearts supporters were already hovering in search of a swift exit.

Those clad in maroon - all 23,000 of them present and the many others in Gorgie - are surely the only beings unmoved by the inimitable Sunshine on Leith.

Newell had his hands on his head. Boyhood Hibee Jason Kerr was holding back the tears. Nicky Cadden was singing from chest. Arm in arm, Hibs were a unit, as they were from the minute they conceded.

"I love these kind of things" - Marink Reedijk on spine-tingling rendition of Sunshine on Leith

At that point, Newell - who proceeded to pull the strings - was full of fear.

A simple but strong header from Claudio Braga, before many supporters had even taken to their seats, brought concern.

Could a repeat of that unforgettable afternoon - Hibs supporters aren't allowed to forget it - 14 years ago, when Hearts fired five past them in the Scottish Cup final, be on the cards?

"The game plan was out the window," midfielder Newell said. "It's not ideal, is it?

"You go to bed [on Saturday night] thinking of all the scenarios and the way you dream and imagine the game is going to go and then, after two minutes, they score.

"But I think, if anything, it shows how good the character is and kind of emphasises it was even more of a special performance, not just the win."

Which is, surely, what Reedijk and his team will take out of this the most. Any team can win a cup game, but not any team can show the grit, determination and depth Hibs did in setting up a final against Rangers next month.

The showpiece is six weeks away. Few clubs more than Hibs know how much can change in that time frame.

They have as many league games in that period, with the last - of course - being a dress rehearsal of the final as they welcome Derek McInnes' side to Easter Road.

While those in green and white admitted post-match it would be difficult not to think of their return to Hampden - when they will be aiming for the club's first silverware since beating the Ibrox side in the 2016 Scottish Cup final - they know they need to arrest their current league form.

With just two wins in 11 games, they have a trip to struggling Aberdeen - who lost in Saturday's semi-final - on Saturday before welcoming both Dundee clubs to the capital.

Trips to Motherwell and Kilmarnock respectively follow before that meeting with the Light Blues as they search for some much-needed points.

The hope is this performance and result will kick-start their quest to climb the table.

"It's huge," 33-year-old Newell added. "You kind of forget that there's a cup final after that, do you know what I mean?

"You feel like you want to say, that's it done because it felt massive. These games are always huge no matter where they are, but we have to kick on now.

"We have to use it and hopefully it gives all the boys confidence, because it should do. We were outstanding."

Do that, and repeat this result against Rangers on 13 December, and Reedijk and co will never be left wanting for music and beer in Leith ever again.

#770. Trailing 8-0 & down to six players - abandoned game labelled a 'farce'

Andover Town had scored seven goals in the first half against Paulsgrove

A non-league game which was abandoned after a side trailing 8-0 were reduced to six players has been labelled "a complete farce".

Andover Town were 8-0 up when their Hampshire Premier League Division One match with Paulsgrove on Saturday had to be called off early in the second half.

Andover boss Robbie Skeates said four Paulsgrove players did not come out after half-time - when the score was 7-0 - and another went off injured after the eighth goal was scored.

The laws of football say a match may not continue if either team has fewer than seven players.

The Hampshire Premier Football League told BBC Sport it is investigating the matter while Paulsgrove, in social media posts, appeared to blame the abandonment on injuries.

Speaking to Andover Town's website,, external Skeates said: "I've been involved in football a long time and I've genuinely never seen anything like what happened today from an opposition side.

"All 11 of their players walked off perfectly fine at half-time with us 7-0 up.

"They eventually came back out with seven, so apparently four must have managed to get injured in the changing room.

"We scored pretty much straight away to make it 8-0 and from there it became a complete farce."

BBC Sport has asked the league for Paulsgrove FC's contact details but that request was declined.

However, several posts on X appearing to come from Paulsgrove's official account claimed the players were all genuinely injured.

One reply to a post from Skeates read: "Sadly can't make injured player [sic] continue".

Skeates said Andover Town would submit a report to the league.

A spokesperson for the Hampshire Premier Football League said: "As is standard for any abandoned game, an investigation is under way and until that process has been completed, we cannot make any comment."

Andover Town are mid-table in the 16-team league, which is in the 12th tier of the English football pyramid.

Paulsgrove are bottom, having lost all 10 games this season, including three completed games where they were beaten by eight goals or more.

#769. Steinmeier in China: A major state visit in uncertain times

President Frank-Walter Steinmeier is traveling to China on a state visit in a period of political and economic uncertainty. Germany is seeking alternative partners in the region but also wants good ties with Beijing.

Eight years have passed since Frank-Walter Steinmeier's last trip to China. Since then, the relationship between China and Europe has changed significantly. The German president plans to spend several days touring China before concluding his visit in Beijing, where he will meet with China's leaders.

His visit comes just as the Chinese Communist Party's Central Committee is convening for its plenary session, a major annual event that foreign dignitaries usually avoid when timing their visits.

The focus of the president's five-day trip will be "Germany's diverse and complex relations with China, as well as the challenges involved," his office said in a statement. In addition to sites of cultural exchange, the itinerary will also include a visit to a Volkswagen plant in Hefei.

The automotive industry, in particular, illustrates the dilemma facing Germany's China policy. China is one of the most important markets for German automotive and machinery manufacturers, as well as for the chemical industry. At the same time, state-supported overcapacity in China is putting pressure on European manufacturers.

Not only that. Germany and Europe are dependent on China for raw materials and technologies, which means they are increasingly seeking out alternative partnerships.

Steinmeier was once an advocate of the policy of "change through trade" — the idea that other countries could be persuaded to become more democratic with the leverage of global trade — which has few adherents left in Germany today.

Now he must now pursue a tougher European line in Beijing. Caught between partnership and competition, Europe leaders recently managed to reach an agreement: Imports of plug-in hybrid vehicles from China are to be scaled back.

"That was a concrete step, but it can only be the beginning," said Michael Laha, an expert on China at the German Council on Foreign Relations (DGAP) in Berlin.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Coinciding with Steinmeier's state visit to China, Chancellor Friedrich Merz is traveling to the Indo-Pacific with business representatives. His visit to Japan, Singapore and South Korea will focus on competitiveness, technological upheavals, defense cooperation and critical raw materials. Merz is visiting companies and attending important regional economic conferences in Tokyo and Seoul.

The dual trips are Berlin's attempt to send a twofold message: While the chancellor is "deliberately strengthening Germany's partnerships in the Indo-Pacific at a time of global upheaval," according to Laha, the president is seeking dialogue with Beijing at a time when Germany and Europe are recalibrating their relationship with China.

"This joint trip sends a very well-coordinated message to the Chinese that we remain committed to the partnership but at the same time are taking steps to reduce risk," said Laha, before adding that this is a difficult balancing act that also allows China to save face.

While Merz will be accompanied by a large economic delegation, Steinmeier will be traveling to China with representatives from German culture, politics, and academia. Mikko Huotari, director of the China Institute MERICS, is also expected to be part of the delegation — even though Beijing has imposed sanctions on the institute. "The fact that he is coming along sends a clear message to the Chinese side that we do not approve of the sanctions," said Laha.

In 2021, the EU imposed sanctions against several Chinese party and regional officials, as well as an organization accused of serious human rights violations and oppressing the Uyghur minority. It was the first time such sanctions had been imposed on China since the Tiananmen Square massacre in 1989, and Beijing did not take kindly to them. In response, the Chinese government imposed entry bans and other sanctions against European politicians, scholars, and institutions, including MERICS.

Laha did not expect human rights to play a major role in the German president's trip. Steinmeier is considered a pragmatist when it comes to China policy. As foreign minister, he distanced himself from his predecessor Joschka Fischer, a critic of China, and even criticized Chancellor Angela Merkel when she hosted the Dalai Lama.

On the subject of Ukraine, Steinmeier is likely to be more direct and raise the issue of China's role in the conflict. "Beijing is clearly on Moscow's side," said Laha. In Berlin, however, officials are convinced that China can do more to persuade Russia to engage in serious negotiations and find a solution to the conflict.

Steinmeier may make this clear in his speech at Peking University on Thursday. Germany has "long viewed China's emergence with respect and goodwill," read a statement from the president's office. Today, however, the focus is less on China's continued rise and more on how it uses its growing power.

"If the president points out that Russia used its power to attack a sovereign state, he could be alluding to another regional connection: Taiwan," said Laha. That could be seen as an appeal to Beijing to assume more responsibility for the regional and international order.

To conclude his visit, Steinmeier will meet with China's leadership in Beijing. Talks are planned with President Xi Jinping, whom he has known for nearly two decades, as well as with Premier Li Qiang and the chairman of the National People's Congress, Zhao Leji.

The trip marks the culmination of Steinmeier's focus on Asia during his second term in office. Since then, he has deliberately sought to forge close ties with partners in the region and has advocated for greater diversification. Now China, which is Germany's most important and most challenging partner, will come to its own conclusion.

This article was originally published in German.

#768. Jack Grealish left out of Everton squad again for Premier League trip to Newcastle

Grealish omitted last Thursday for disciplinary reasons

Playmaker left on Merseyside to work on his fitness

Jack Grealish is poised to miss his third successive game for Everton when David Moyes’s side visit Newcastle in the Premier League on Monday night.

Grealish was dropped from Everton’s Carabao Cup win against Matthias Jaissle’s team last Thursday for disciplinary reasons. The 31-year-old had missed training without permission in the buildup to the fourth-round tie. He was also absent from the previous game, a Premier League defeat at Arsenal, owing to illness.

Everton have travelled to the north-east without the playmaker, who rejoined the club on a second lucrative loan deal from Manchester City this summer.

#765. Suki Waterhouse Addresses Robert Pattinson Marriage Rumors

Suki Waterhouse set the record straight on rumors that she and fiancé Robert Pattinson secretly tied the knot after nearly a decade together.

Suki Waterhouse and Robert Pattinson are waiting for the prime time to say “I do.”

Despite past speculation that the couple privately married, the “Back in Love” singer confirmed she and the Primetime actor have yet to tie the knot, but shared details about their plans for a potential wedding.

“It would either be all or nothing,” Waterhouse told the Sunday Times in an interview published Nov. 1. “If we were going to go for it we’d have a massive party, blow it out.”

The Daisy Jones & The Six star—who began dating Pattinson in 2018, and became engaged in 2023—added that if a wedding were to take place, it wouldn’t be until next year, pointing to the couple’s busy schedules and a lack of a consistent home base.

In fact, since Waterhouse, 34, and Pattinson, 40, welcomed their baby girl in March 2024, they have called multiple places around the world home, including London, New York and Los Angeles.

“Our life since having our daughter, which is strange and backwards, hasn’t been anywhere,” Waterhouse shared. “We’ve been in rentals and moving every couple of months and we just haven’t been home.”

“It’s been wherever we can base ourselves,” she added, “and wherever we can stay together as a family.”

While the “Good Looking” artist and Twilight alum’s family life may look a bit different than most due to their careers, Waterhouse is so grateful for the bond they’ve built.

“It is almost a decade [of our relationship] and that is a beautiful thing,” she explained. “It’s a thing that I go, I can’t believe that I have this in my life and I can’t believe that I’m so happy. And maybe I was surprised because before I had only ever gone out with someone for two years and if it was two years it would have been a disaster at the end.”

And though Waterhouse and Pattinson keep most details about their personal lives rather private—including not publicly disclosing their daughter’s name—she did share a sweet update on their parenthood journey.

“I’m two and a half years into motherhood now,” she shared. “I feel very confident that we’re great parents and juggling a slightly abnormal life, but I feel good about how we’re doing it and we are both just so connected to her. She’s such a wonderful, happy girl.”

For a closer look at Waterhouse and Pattinson’s romance, keep reading…

Suki Waterhouse and Robert Pattinson first sparked relationship speculation in July 2018, when they were photographed on a PDA-filled date night in London.

In Dec. 2022, the private pair made their relationship red carpet official at Dior's fashion show in Egypt...

...where they couldn't help but show off their love.

The Daisy Jones actress and the Twilight alum turned the 2023 Met Gala into a date night on the first Monday in May.

The couple attended GO Campaign's 17th annual GO Gala at Citizen News in Hollywood on Oct. 21.

About two weeks after Suki confirmed her pregnancy, she and Rob went to the Poor Things premiere in New York. And they weren't the only stars there as Taylor Swift was also at the event.

In February 2023, Suki shared rare insight into her relationship with Rob. "I'm always incredibly excited when I see his name pop up [on my phone] or even a text, and I think he feels the same about me," she told The Sunday Times. "We've always got so much to say, and I find him hilarious."

"Rob definitely isn't getting advice from me about acting," Suki shared with The Sunday Times, "but of course I'll try and get him to help me with an audition before he falls asleep on the sofa."

The singer introduced the couple's baby on Instagram April 4, writing, "welcome to the world angel."

The pair made their first official joint appearance since welcoming their daugher Oct. 5, 2024 at the Veuve Clicquot Polo Classic in Pacific Palisades, Calif.

#764. From Fleetwood embarrassment to 'magical' Anfield win 14 years in making

Arsenal move clear at the top with a rare win at Liverpool

That is what manager Mikel Arteta said before Arsenal secured their first Premier League win at Anfield in 14 years, beating Liverpool thanks to Kai Havertz's first-half goal.

Arteta was Arsenal captain the last time the Gunners won at Liverpool - 2-0 in 2012 - and they have had 16 unsuccessful trips in all competitions until Sunday's victory.

The Spaniard's side, as they so often do, produced a defensive masterclass to keep out wave after wave of Liverpool attack to deliver a rare and historic win.

Arsenal travelled to Anfield after an embarrassing loss to League Two Fleetwood Town in the Carabao Cup on Tuesday. Arteta said he thought that humbling loss in Lancashire could spur his side on to a historic win at Liverpool.

"Extremely proud. It's been 14 years, that's a long time," Arteta said after the game.

"I'm sure we made everybody attached to the club extremely proud today. Not only for the victory but for the way we've done it, the spirit we've shown.

"Especially considering what happened four days ago when you lose and go out of the cup against a team you are supposed to beat. That's the magical part of this game, it can take you to really bad places but four days later you have the opportunity to do something really historic and we've done it.

"Overall, to win against a team that is producing what they are doing, and also in the emotional state after Fleetwood, that's what a winning team should do."

Before the match, centre-back Gabriel said that Arsenal were expecting a "big battle" and "big chaos" against Liverpool.

That prediction was correct and, after going ahead, Arsenal were pinned back before the break.

Although the second half was a bit calmer, they still defended resolutely and did not allow Liverpool a shot on target.

The Gunners, who have kept six clean sheets this season, are now three points clear at the top of the table after nine games.

Rice is a rounded midfielder, but could be more selfish - Murphy

I'll tell my players to dive in future - Iraola

Arsenal's 24 points is the most by any team after nine games of a season since the Gunners themselves in 2022-23.

And only in the 2004-05 and 2007-08 seasons have Arsenal had more at this stage of a Premier League season.

"It means a lot to our football club," match winner Havertz said after the win.

"It's been 13 games [in the Premier League without a win here], its a crazy stat and it's what the fans deserve. We are happy we gave them that."

The win was also the first time that Arsenal had kept a clean sheet at Anfield in the Premier League since that victory in 2012.

Rice analyses how Arsenal won at Liverpool

"That is the Anfield way, that is what this Liverpool team can do, this is what this stadium does to you," Declan Rice - who assisted Havertz's goal - added. "It just creates waves and waves of attack.

"We've not won here in 14 years. It was relentless attacks but in the end that way we stuck together, that togetherness we have is undefeated. It's nothing like I've ever seen before."

Rice has been one of Arsenal's standout players this season and has five assists in the league already

'He's been fantastic' - Konsa signing a success for Arsenal

Arsenal are now two points better off after nine games of this campaign than last season, when they won the title.

The Gunners attack is not yet flowing and they have scored just 14 league goals in nine games

Arteta has been restricted with his options in the forward line with Bukayo Saka out injured, 16-year-old Max Dowman suspended after his red card at Fleetwood, Christos Tzolis just back from a hamstring injury, and Viktor Gyokeres and Havertz both struggling for form.

But the Arsenal defence is an elite unit.

The back four only conceded 27 goals last season and, on this performance, they could once again be the difference for the Gunners.

"I'm extremely proud; this is something you want to accomplish." Arteta said after being asked what the win against Liverpool means to him.

"That's the challenge and mission you want to accomplish. I love it when it's something we have not done for many years.

"It was the same with Chelsea away and Manchester United away. To be able to beat all those, that's the purpose and motivation and why we do what we do."

Manchester City are second in the table but are waiting to find out what happens, pending their appeal, following their charge for breaching the Premier League financial rules.

And with the rest of the big-name sides in the league in a period of transition, Arsenal could find themselves with a healthy lead at the top of the table of the table if things carry on as they are.

#763. WSL talking points: Kang could have a problem and how long can Slegers hang on?

Arsenal dropped points again despite dominating while Lauren James had to go off in Chelsea’s 6-0 win at Charlton

London City Lionesses may have lost 2-1 to champions Manchester City, but their performances and league position have shown their European aspirations are far from unrealistic. Aided by Arsenal’s poor start, London City are third in the WSL table and were frustrated to end the day with a six-point gap to the top two after dominating in Bromley. “It’s doubly frustrating, because I think the result was not the one we deserve,” said their coach, Eder Maestre. “Manchester City are more mature. They are more used to it. When you have this consistency and you are very used to playing these kinds of games, maybe you have more experience.” Maestre’s team have a three-point lead over fourth-placed Tottenham and if they continue their upwards trajectory and qualify for the Champions League, Uefa will be forced to tackle the possible scenario of two Michelle Kang-owned clubs, London City and OL Lyonnes, qualifying sooner than they perhaps anticipated. Suzanne Wrack

Match report: London City Lionesses 1-2 Manchester City

It was groundhog day for Arsenal against Aston Villa with the Gunners going a goal down for the fifth time this season. “We just said it feels like we’re playing the same game over and over again,” said the manager, Renée Slegers. “We go one goal down from a break and we don’t start with enough urgency.” The issue for Arsenal is that opposition teams can sense this lack of urgency. Get one chance early on, take it and then capitalise on the fact that Slegers’ side just cannot break down a low block. How Slegers, her staff and the squad arrest this malaise is the big unanswered question. The wins against Tottenham and Benfica felt like the seeds of a turnaround in fortunes, but they papered over cracks that will be exposed again until they make more of their dominance in the final third. SW

WSL roundup: Arsenal stall against Villa despite Russo strike

There is significant concern over Lauren James’s fitness after she suffered another injury against Charlton. The 25-year-old was forced off the pitch after pulling up off the ball in the 35th minute. “It is difficult to say,” the Chelsea manager, Sonia Bompastor, said. “I can only say it’s her hamstring and we’ll assess her later to have more detailed information.” It is the latest fitness worry for the England international who, after being limited to just 11 and six league starts in the last two campaigns respectively, had started this season in superb form with four goals in the WSL. It was the only blemish on an otherwise enjoyable afternoon for the league leaders who ran out 6-0 winners at the Valley. Defender Nathalie Björn marked her first start after months on the sidelines with the opener. Substitute Aggie Beever-Jones ended her barren spell, scoring her first league goal since September 2025. There was also an emotional moment for the young Italian midfielder Giulia Dragoni who opened her Chelsea account after coming off the bench. Sophie Downey

WSL roundup: James injured in Chelsea’s win over Charlton

As she led Tottenham out at St Andrew’s, Drew Spence wrote herself into the history books. Her start against Birmingham marked her 217th in the WSL, making her the competition’s new all-time record appearance maker. It is the latest accolade of a decorated career that has seen her win five league titles, four FA Cups and two League Cups. The 34-year-old Jamaica international featured in the inaugural WSL season back in 2011 with Chelsea where she spent 14 years before switching to Spurs in 2022. She was once again at the heart of Martin Ho’s midfield as Tottenham ended their three-game losing streak with a dominant 4-1 win over Birmingham. Spurs were back to their attacking best, registering 11 of their 29 shots on target, recording 61 touches in the opposition box and having four different goalscorers. The victory moves them up to fourth in the table. SD

Viviane Asseyi put on a performance Zinedine Zidane would be proud of as West Ham stormed to a dominant 4-1 victory against Liverpool. The 32-year-old scored twice for the Hammers on Sunday, the second goal a brilliant free-kick from the edge of the box which flew into the top-right corner. Asseyi told the Guardian recently that she grew up wanting to be like the former France international – and that excellent strike was Zidane-esque. Her double in east London took the forward up to five goals for the season, moving her to joint fifth in the Golden Boot race. “She missed a hat-trick unfortunately but I’m very happy,” the West Ham head coach, Rita Guarino, said. “She’s an incredible player. Very happy for her, very happy in the way the team help her to make this kind of performance.” Emillia Hawkins

No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football

Is creativity a problem for both of these sides? On Saturday’s evidence, yes. Both sides looked well-drilled from a defensive standpoint but this was about as textbook a 0-0 as you could imagine, with both sides registering an expected goals (xG) of under 0.5 and – according to the WSL’s official website – neither of them having any “big chances” in the game. Everton are now the joint-second lowest goalscorers in the division – only bottom-placed Charlton have scored fewer – and Manchester United are only two goals better off themselves. The leaders Chelsea have netted three times as many league goals as Manchester United’s nine already. Perhaps both of these clubs ought to be targeting inventive players with ingenuity and flair in January, to offer them a bit more unpredictability going forward. Tom Garry

Match report: Everton 0-0 Manchester United

The Brighton head coach, Arturo Ruiz, praised the team’s togetherness after they came from behind to beat Crystal Palace 2-1. “It’s a team win. All the players deserve today,” he said. “I don’t think that there’s one player that was much better than the others, and that’s the best thing that a team can have.” The victory moves Brighton up to sixth and they now have three straight home wins for the first time since September 2021. “As I always say, we play for the fans, we play for our people, and the three points are for them because they always support us in the best way,” Ruiz added. Palace lost but it would be remiss not to mention Annabel Blanchard’s goal for the visitors, a superbly taken long-range effort in the 34th minute. Marcus Christenson

#762. Hellberg unsure of 'brilliant' Lankshear's England chances

Will Lankshear has only played the whole match in four of Middlesbrough's 13 Championship games

Middlesbrough head coach Kim Hellberg says he has too many other things to worry about than whether or not Will Lankshear receives a surprise England call-up.

Lankshear scored two more in the 3-0 win over Charlton Athletic to take his tally for Boro to 15 in 16 games, in all competitions, as they cemented their place at the top of the Championship.

The 21-year-old has claimed 13 strikes in as many Championship appearances following his summer move from Tottenham and Boro's form and his goalscoring exploits are receiving wider acclaim.

Last month England head coach Thomas Tuchel said he would never rule out picking players not in the top flight with their clubs, furthering the possibility that Lankshear could make the squad on Friday for the Nations League fixtures with Spain and Croatia later this month.

"I have no clue," said Hellberg, when asked if he thought Lankshear would find himself in Tuchel's reckoning.

"I have so many things to think about in terms of my own squad in terms of ins and outs and I have a brilliant squad working so hard so I let other people worry about that one."

The 'Kane-esque' striker Spurs may regret letting go

Lankshear has scored in all but one of his appearances at the Riverside and has scored two goals in four different matches.

Since the international break in September ended, he has been on fire, scoring seven times in five matches, including four in his last two in the victories over Bolton Wanderers and then Charlton Athletic.

The leading English scorer in the Premier League is Morgan Rogers with five, predominantly an attacking midfielder for Chelsea, while the English striker with most goals is Leeds United's Dominic Calvert-Lewin with four.

Lankshear even has more goals this season than England captain and Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane, who has netted 12 in 14 games for Bayern Munich and the national team.

The Boro forward was part of the England Under-21 side last month, and Hellberg reckons he is already a better player than the one who moved to Teesside in the summer.

"Will is fantastic," the Swede told BBC Radio Tees. "He does everything every day. You can see the improvements through the season.

"When he arrived, he was unbelievable in the 18-yard box, and then he added on qualities in his defensive game that we worked with and pushed him to do, which he has done brilliantly and I am so happy with him getting a goal [against Charlton] from pressing high. He's a brilliant lad."
